5 Things I Did to 
Lose 44 lbs (20 kg)

original_client_text.markup_text:
A year ago, I weighed 72 kg. Today, I’m around 55 kg. In total, I’ve lost about 44 lbs (20 kg) since having my second baby.

And the most interesting part? I finally started seeing results when I stopped trying to do EVERYTHING at once.

I used to work out a lot, eat healthy, and still struggle with my weight.

These 5 changes are what actually transformed my body:

1. I FOCUSED ON REAL STRENGTH TRAINING.

3 workouts a week, the same core exercises, and I progressively increased the weights instead of constantly adding more exercises.

Squats, Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts, and step-ups.

MUSCLE is what changed my body shape, not sweating more.

2. I STOPPED RELYING ONLY ON “CLEAN EATING” AND STARTED PAYING ATTENTION TO CALORIES AND MACROS.

Just because you’re eating healthy foods doesn’t mean you’re in a calorie deficit.

Once I started paying attention to how much I was eating, including protein, fats, and carbs, I could finally understand where those extra calories were coming from.

3. I PUT PROTEIN FIRST AT EVERY MEAL.

My goal is 120–150g of protein a day!

In practice, that means eggs, fish, meat, chicken, and seafood.

I always prioritize getting enough protein before adding everything else to my plate.

It keeps me full longer and helps me maintain the muscle I’ve worked so hard to build.

I LOVE protein, so eating this way is perfect for ME!

4. I ATE IN A SMALL CALORIE DEFICIT AND STOPPED STARTING OVER EVERY MONDAY.

Around 300–400 calories below maintenance.

A small deficit is something you can actually stick to long-term.

That’s what finally helped me stop constantly struggling with my weight.

One meal that doesn’t fit your usual routine is NOT a reason to start all over again.

5. I WALKED EVERY SINGLE DAY.

10,000 steps.

Over a week, walking adds up to a significant amount of extra movement and calorie expenditure.

And for me, it doesn’t leave me starving the way intense cardio sessions sometimes did.

WHAT I DIDN’T DO:

I didn’t train 6 days a week or force myself to do endless cardio.

I chose simple, real food, strength training, and daily movement.

I also weighed myself regularly, measured my waist, and tracked changes in my body.

The scale can stay the same for weeks while your waist gets smaller and your clothes start fitting completely differently.

And I did all of this at 37.

Today, I still follow these same 5 principles.

💛 Follow @nataly_run for more and SAVE this post!

#weightlossjourneys #fatloss #weightlossafter40 #strengthtraining #highprotein

aweme_info.desc: DISCLAIMER: This video is NOT intended to give weight-loss advice, encourage weight loss, or suggest that cutting out gluten will make you lose weight. I’m simply sharing my personal experience because, for a long time, I knew something was going on with my body. Despite trying calorie deficits, exercising, and doing all the things I thought I was supposed to do, I was still struggling with unexplained symptoms, inflammation, and changes in my weight. After discovering that gluten may have been contributing to my symptoms, I made changes to my diet and started prioritizing my gut health and overall well-being. Since then, I’ve experienced significant changes in how I look and, more importantly, how I FEEL. What worked for me will not necessarily work for you. Cutting out gluten is not a magic weight-loss solution, nor is it necessary or beneficial for everyone. Our bodies, health histories, and nutritional needs are all different. I’m sharing this because sometimes the answer isn’t eating less, exercising more, or trying harder. Sometimes it’s worth investigating whether there’s an underlying health issue that needs attention. My goal was never to encourage anyone to lose 20 pounds. It was to figure out why my body wasn’t feeling or functioning the way it should. Please don’t take my experience as medical advice or a reason to eliminate entire food groups without understanding your own body’s needs. Work with a qualified healthcare professional if you’re experiencing similar symptoms. I use @micaela riley / nutritionist and have had the best experience so far!! #weightloss

original_client_text.markup_text:
DISCLAIMER: This video is NOT intended to give weight-loss advice, encourage weight loss, or suggest that cutting out gluten will make you lose weight.

I’m simply sharing my personal experience because, for a long time, I knew something was going on with my body. Despite trying calorie deficits, exercising, and doing all the things I thought I was supposed to do, I was still struggling with unexplained symptoms, inflammation, and changes in my weight.

After discovering that gluten may have been contributing to my symptoms, I made changes to my diet and started prioritizing my gut health and overall well-being. Since then, I’ve experienced significant changes in how I look and, more importantly, how I FEEL.

What worked for me will not necessarily work for you. Cutting out gluten is not a magic weight-loss solution, nor is it necessary or beneficial for everyone. Our bodies, health histories, and nutritional needs are all different.

I’m sharing this because sometimes the answer isn’t eating less, exercising more, or trying harder. Sometimes it’s worth investigating whether there’s an underlying health issue that needs attention.

My goal was never to encourage anyone to lose 20 pounds. It was to figure out why my body wasn’t feeling or functioning the way it should.

Please don’t take my experience as medical advice or a reason to eliminate entire food groups without understanding your own body’s needs. Work with a qualified healthcare professional if you’re experiencing similar symptoms.
I use @micaela riley / nutritionist and have had the best experience so far!! #weightloss

Sometimes the answer isn’t another diet, another workout plan, or someone telling you to “just be more disciplined.” Sometimes the real work is figuring out what keeps making it so hard for YOU to stay consistent in the first place. Your habits. Your patterns. Your environment. Your mindset. Your life. Once you understand those pieces, you can stop trying to force yourself into somebody else’s strategy and start building one that actually works for you long-term. Simple doesn’t always mean easy. aweme_info.desc: When we see weight loss transformations, we usually see the physical changes. Someone going from one size to another, their before and after pictures, and how different they look. But we rarely talk about what happens mentally. We don’t talk about the confidence you lose when you’re uncomfortable in your body, avoiding pictures, feeling self-conscious in social settings or struggling to feel good about yourself. We don’t talk about the frustration of putting in the work and not seeing results, comparing yourself to others or how exhausting it can become mentally. Weight loss is more than a physical journey. It can affect your confidence, happiness and relationship with yourself. And that’s a side of the journey we need to talk about, too. #onepercentbyving #Fitness #weightlosstransformation #MentalHealth #blowthisup

DO YOU GET IT THOUGH?

original_client_text.markup_text:
When we see weight loss transformations, we usually see the physical changes. Someone going from one size to another, their before and after pictures, and how different they look.

But we rarely talk about what happens mentally.

We don’t talk about the confidence you lose when you’re uncomfortable in your body, avoiding pictures, feeling self-conscious in social settings or struggling to feel good about yourself.

We don’t talk about the frustration of putting in the work and not seeing results, comparing yourself to others or how exhausting it can become mentally.

Weight loss is more than a physical journey. It can affect your confidence, happiness and relationship with yourself.

And that’s a side of the journey we need to talk about, too.

#onepercentbyving #Fitness #weightlosstransformation #MentalHealth #blowthisup
